clue.text: Share a roll, being a reasonable person

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share or allowance
a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly splitting a bread roll with a companion, being fair about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread, but it is a register of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of reason over faith or emotion is a reasonable person in the philosophical sense.

clue.text: Apply balm or aggravate someone's trouble

definitions.meaning: to massage an ointment into the skin
the idiom for dwelling on another's misfortune to make them feel worse

explanation.surface: A choice between soothing a sore and making it worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means massaging ointment into skin and idiomatically means harping on someone's mistake.

clue.text: Official charge is for transportation

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied by government

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on the cost of getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabs for hire are a form of transportation; the plural here names several vehicles.

clue.text: Pro wins, he is out for a title

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A professional wins a match and is out to claim the championship title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PRO WINS HE; 'is' and 'for a' are links. The sporting 'title' is really legal title to property.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, title is the right of possession of property, which is the same thing as legal possession.

clue.text: Excellent detective gives assistance

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the figure 1 is read as the letter I
DS is the abbreviation for detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A brilliant detective lends a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 ('Excellent') becomes AI by reading the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone is to give them assistance; the verb form matches 'gives'.

clue.text: Cite ways to develop arctic wilderness

indicators.note: developing something changes its form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to name routes for opening up polar land.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen barren expanse is what an arctic wilderness looks like.

clue.text: Twitch at first to wake in confusion

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it
in confusion means the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sleeper jerks awake, muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitch at first' tempts you to take T from 'Twitch', but 'Twitch' is the definition; 'at first' works on 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a sharp pull or jerk, a twitch.

clue.text: Gymnast will need this money in the bank

definitions.meaning: the poise that keeps a gymnast steady on the beam
the amount held in a bank account

explanation.surface: A gymnast needing savings, as though the sport were costly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both steadiness of the body and the sum standing in an account.

clue.text: New broadcast leaves out 500 performers

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves out means a letter is dropped from the word broadcast

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A new programme that cuts 500 performers from its cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves out' drops D (500) from BROADCAST to leave ROACBAST, which 'New' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus tumblers and trapeze artists are performers.

clue.text: Time to pack up after Christmas?

definitions.text: Time to pack up after Christmas?

parts.words: Time to pack up after Christmas?
parts.note: the day after Christmas read as a day for putting things in boxes

explanation.surface: Wondering when to clear away the decorations after the festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: The name has nothing to do with packing; it probably comes from Christmas boxes, gifts given to servants. 26 December is a British public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The holiday on 26 December falls right after Christmas and plays on putting things in boxes.

clue.text: We hear forty of the Romans do better

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Forty Romans outperforming everyone, as rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, to do better than they do.

clue.text: Weapons carried by police that may produce stares

indicators.note: may produce says the letters can be reworked to make a new word

explanation.surface: Police stun guns that draw startled looks from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards in the surface: the answer may be rearranged to produce STARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric stun guns are carried by many police forces as weapons.

clue.text: Face up! It might mean the opposite!

definitions.text: Face up! It might mean the opposite!

parts.words: Face up! It might mean the opposite!
parts.note: to face up to something is to confront it; the opposite is to retreat, and read literally the answer pairs back against face and down against up

explanation.surface: A command to confront things, with a warning it may mean the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreating from a position is the opposite of confronting it, and the words are literal opposites of face and up.

clue.text: Go and hunt out duck

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to go and track down a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman's duck is a score of zero, so the word for zero fits.

clue.text: Last of a multi-tea blend

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The final cup of a mixed-leaf tea blend.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means final, coming last in a series.

clue.text: Accommodation for poor sailors?

parts.note: the cheapest ship's quarters, for passengers who could not afford better; 'sailors' means those who sail as passengers, not crew

explanation.surface: Wondering where hard-up seamen sleep aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor sailors' suggests bad seamen or crew, but it means passengers of little means.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-fare section of a passenger ship housed travellers who could not pay for cabins.

clue.text: Mum let one out for profit

indicators.note: out here means put into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother rented a room out to make some money.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary, fee or gain from employment, which is a profit.

clue.text: Split seen in a flirty dress?

definitions.meaning: a division or splitting apart, as in a crystal's planes
the hollow between a woman's breasts on show in a low-cut dress

explanation.surface: A tear spotted in a revealing dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a splitting apart and the neckline view a low-cut dress reveals.

clue.text: Stone pitcher

parts.note: read as a jug made of stone, but meaning a device that hurls stones

explanation.surface: A jug made of stoneware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitcher' looks like a jug; it is a thrower.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege engine or forked sling flings stones, so it pitches them.

clue.text: Fabulous site desert inhabitant returned to

parts.note: a camel lives in the desert

indicators.note: returned means the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A desert creature heading back to a legendary place.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's court belongs to legend, so it is a site from fable.

clue.text: Production of smaller woods for indoor bowls

definitions.text: Production of smaller woods for indoor bowls

parts.words: Production of smaller woods for indoor bowls
parts.note: read as making small bowling balls (woods) for the indoor game, but meaning growing miniature trees in pots

explanation.surface: Making scaled-down woods for the indoor version of lawn bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: In British lawn bowls the balls are called woods; here woods are trees and bowls are pots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of growing dwarf trees in shallow pots produces smaller trees for indoor dishes.

clue.text: Enlist round about end of May, showing panache

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
round suggests turning the letters around, so the word is rearranged
end of asks for the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Signing up at the close of May with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges ENLIST into INSTLE, and 'about' puts it around Y (the last letter of May).
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with flair and elegance is the same as showing panache.

clue.text: Reminder one's given in passing

parts.note: 'in passing' suggests casually, but means on dying: a monument that keeps someone in mind after death

explanation.surface: A casual nudge someone drops while walking by.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument or ceremony keeps the dead in mind, a reminder granted when someone passes away.

clue.text: Outsize rubbish has been stacked around hen house

indicators.note: stacked around says one piece is piled round another, enclosing it

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
OS is the abbreviation for outsize clothing

explanation.surface: Junk piled up around the chicken coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the perch or shelter where hens settle for the night.

clue.text: Measures broken biscuit (one I left)

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled
left here means departed, so a letter goes from the word

parts.note: one of the two letters I in the word

explanation.surface: A broken biscuit, with the bracket saying one piece was left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes one I out of BISCUIT to give BSCUIT, which 'broken' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length based on the forearm, so cubits are measures.

clue.text: Perfect thought comes to pupil

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student hits on an excellent idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as good as could be wished.

clue.text: A major landmass, though it could be minor

definitions.text: A major landmass, though it could be minor

parts.words: A major landmass, though it could be minor
parts.note: the largest continent, which with 'Minor' added names the Anatolian peninsula of ancient times

explanation.surface: A big landmass that could equally be described as small.
explanation.walkthrough: Asia Minor is the old name for Anatolia, most of modern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent is a major landmass, and the classical name for Anatolia adds 'Minor' to it.

clue.text: Dismiss and discuss no further

definitions.meaning: to drop a subject and stop arguing about it

explanation.surface: A boss sacking someone and then refusing to talk about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both releasing an employee and dropping a topic.

clue.text: Planned a Yule rest with no frills

indicators.note: planned suggests arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone scheduled a plain, quiet Christmas break.
explanation.definitionFit: Done severely and plainly, without decoration, is done with no frills.

clue.text: French fortress as the HQ, until being captured

indicators.note: being captured says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: headquarters is a base
till means until

explanation.surface: A fortress serving as headquarters until it fell to attackers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789 is the most famous French fortress.
